governanceNotes: D1 batch 46 (2026-09-24): one bounded direct-causation edge authored - hyperinsulinism to hypoglycemia (rank 1), DIRECT_CAUSATION with etiologicalConsensus PROBABLE, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment AT_LEAST_AS_LIKELY_AS_NOT, hypothesizedOnly:false, and mechanismCategory METABOLIC_OR_NUTRITIONAL. The proposition rests on the Demirbilek 2017 congenital-hyperinsulinism diagnosis and treatment update, which states that hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia is the inappropriate secretion of insulin in the presence of low plasma glucose and leads to severe and persistent hypoglycaemia, and that insulin's inhibitory effect on lipolysis and ketogenesis suppresses ketone-body formation and heightens hypoglycaemic brain injury, and on the Giri 2021 congenital-hyperinsulinism update, which describes unregulated insulin release leading to hypoglycaemia as the most frequent cause of persistent and severe hypoglycaemia in the neonatal period and early childhood. The pathway (β-cell insulin excess -> suppressed hepatic glucose output and enhanced tissue glucose uptake -> hypoglycaemia) is a well-established proximate mechanism rather than a merely statistical association, so a probable nexus is recorded; individual nexus still requires documented hyperinsulinism, a compatible insulin-glucose or C-peptide profile during the hypoglycaemic event, chronology, and exclusion of competing mechanisms.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no diabetes-mellitus or diabetes-mellitus-type-2 edge - hyperinsulinism through inappropriate insulin excess produces hypoglycaemia rather than hyperglycaemia, and the diabetes identities author their own windows from their own primaries (duplicate-scope and direction guards); (ii) no insulin-resistance-syndrome edge - that identity is a distinct sibling whose direction runs to diabetes-mellitus-type-2, and no condition-specific hyperinsulinism-primary data link the two (duplicate-scope guard); (iii) no cognitive-disorder or seizure-disorder edge - the located reviews document hypoglycaemic brain injury and neurodisability, but the cognitive and seizure windows belong to their own primaries and hypoglycaemia is the intermediate node, so a further hyperinsulinism-to-cognition edge would double-count the same pathway (intermediate-chain and duplicate-scope guards; revisit as a two-hop pathway if governance wants the hyperinsulinism -> hypoglycemia -> cognitive-disorder chain expressed); (iv) no obesity or metabolic-syndrome edge - no obesity identity exists and metabolic-syndrome owns its own windows (wrong-target guard); (v) no pancreatic or malignancy edge - insulinoma is a distinct identity with its own potential windows and the generic hyperinsulinism edge does not absorb it (duplicate-scope guard).

nexusClaim.etiologicalTrigger: Documented hyperinsulinism (inappropriate insulin secretion, whether congenital-channel/genetic or otherwise established) -> insulin excess suppresses hepatic glucose output and drives tissue glucose uptake while antagonising counter-regulatory lipolysis and ketogenesis -> claimed hypoglycaemia when the individual insulin-glucose profile, glucose documentation, chronology, and competing mechanisms support that pathway.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Inappropriate pancreatic β-cell insulin secretion in the presence of low plasma glucose drives glucose out of the circulation by suppressing hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis and by promoting insulin-sensitive tissue uptake, and the same insulin excess suppresses lipolysis, ketogenesis, and counter-regulatory responses, so the low glucose is not offset by alternative fuel generation - the metabolic pathway documented in the Demirbilek 2017 congenital-hyperinsulinism update (which frames hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia as inappropriate insulin secretion at low glucose with suppressed ketone-body formation) and in the Giri 2021 update (unregulated insulin release leading to hypoglycaemia); this supports a probable nexus when the individual insulin-glucose profile, glucose documentation, and chronology are compatible.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: In medically conservative terms, the evidence supports the nexus at the at-least-as-likely-as-not level for this individual's presentation: inappropriate insulin secretion at low plasma glucose is the established proximate mechanism of hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia, documented at review level across two independent congenital-hyperinsulinism updates, so when the individual record documents hyperinsulinism and a compatible insulin-glucose profile the pathway is coherent; case-specific review must still confirm the insulin-glucose relationship during the event and exclude competing hypoglycaemia mechanisms, and the edge does not assert an individual nexus without that documentation.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documentation of hyperinsulinism (plasma insulin, C-peptide, or proinsulin during a spontaneous or provoked hypoglycaemic episode; relevant genetic testing; or histopathology where available); documentation of hypoglycaemia with the glucose value, timing, and sampling conditions; chronology linking the hyperinsulinism to the hypoglycaemic episodes; assessment of counter-regulatory status (cortisol, growth hormone, glucagon) and of hepatic, renal, and nutritional status; review of medication or exogenous-insulin exposure; endocrinology assessment of whether the hyperinsulinism materially caused the individual hypoglycaemia
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Insulinoma or other insulin-secreting pancreatic lesion

suggestions.rationale: Authored at DIRECT_CAUSATION with etiologicalConsensus PROBABLE: two independent congenital-hyperinsulinism reviews document that inappropriate insulin secretion at low plasma glucose leads to severe and persistent hypoglycaemia, with insulin additionally suppressing lipolysis and ketogenesis so that alternative fuels are unavailable - a textbook proximate metabolic pathway rather than a statistical association; individual nexus still requires documented hyperinsulinism, a compatible insulin-glucose profile during the hypoglycaemic event, chronology, and exclusion of exogenous insulin, counter-regulatory deficiency, organ failure, and insulinoma.
